source: The brief Kyle pasted on 2026-11-08 from the app at build e3fc8a7 (src unchanged since dc34856), recorded with --write and checked against the paste field by field: header, counts, judgment, profile, the 5 signals, the 3 patterns and their 8 example lines, the distribution and the 21 provenance entries.

header.genreNote: Read as research from an interested publisher: held to research reporting standards, with its own data graded as self-reported.

brief.verdict: This research report makes 397 claims, 16 of them strongly stated; of these, 212 rest on no cited evidence, 5 cite sources too weak to carry them, and 23 claim more cause than the study design supports.

evidenceMap.dek: 263 of 397 claims cite nothing, and 211 of them are stated more firmly than no source can carry. 7 more describe its methods, which the engine does not judge.

rows.sub: read as its own result; nothing cited; graded third-party / analyst
in the sentence, not attached to the claim
no citation, link, quote or named source

panel.provenance: Stated as absolute, with no citation, to the publisher itself. Unsourced carries up to hedged under the corporate standard, so the claim is stated 3 steps past its reach.
panel.note: The engine looked for a citation marker, a footnote, a link or DOI, or a citation in the same sentence, and found none.

howJudged.scenario: Research published by a firm or interest group
howJudged.why: Its findings come from a publisher with a stake in them: they count as self-reported until a third party or peer review checks them.

profile.designCeiling: Licenses up to associational language and weak advice.

signals.title: Register mismatch
signals.summary: Adopts a research-like register, yet 16 of 16 top-tier claims fall short of independent (third-party or audited) evidence — marketing in a lab coat.

signals.title: Reporting gaps
signals.summary: For a cross sectional study, the report does not state: response rate; weighting; missing data or sample-size accounting; data availability.
evidence: missing data or sample-size accounting — STROBE 12c, 13 · AXIS 14

signals.title: Limitations absent
signals.summary: No limitations or caveats passage was found — the paper does not bound its own claims.

signals.title: Interest disclosure
signals.summary: States who sponsored the work or what interest its publisher holds.

patterns.name: Unsupported assertion
patterns.description: A polished, quotable sentence that reads like a settled conclusion but cites little or nothing. The confidence is rhetorical, not evidential — the line carries no backing a reader could check.

patterns.name: Overconfident relative to source
patterns.description: The claim does cite a source, but asserts more certainty than that grade of evidence can carry — the language outruns what the citation actually establishes.

patterns.name: Causal overreach
patterns.description: The claim asserts more cause — or gives firmer advice — than the study design behind it can license. A survey or uncontrolled comparison can show that things move together, not that one produces the other.

brief.distributionNote: How this document's claims spread across the corporate ladder, strongest evidence to unsourced.

entries.criterion: industry sponsorship and favourable results and conclusions
entries.citation: Lundh, A., Lexchin, J., Mintzes, B., Schroll, J. B. & Bero, L. (2017). Industry sponsorship and research outcome. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, 2017(2), MR000033.

entries.criterion: disclosing sources of support and conflicts of interest
entries.citation: International Committee of Medical Journal Editors — Recommendations for the Conduct, Reporting, Editing and Publication of Scholarly Work in Medical Journals, §II.B: Disclosure of Financial and Non-Financial Relationships and Activities, and Conflicts of Interest (updated January 2026).

entries.citation: American Association for Public Opinion Research — Transparency Initiative; Code of Professional Ethics and Practices (rev. April 2021), §III.A.2 “Who Sponsored the Research and Who Conducted It”.
